questions.stem: During melting, the temperature of a pure substance remains constant even though energy is being supplied. Why?

options.text: The energy is being lost to the surroundings
The energy is used to break intermolecular bonds, not to increase kinetic energy
The thermometer is not working correctly during melting
The substance stops absorbing energy during melting

questions.explanation: During a change of state, the energy supplied goes into breaking (or weakening) the bonds between particles rather than increasing their kinetic energy. Since temperature measures average kinetic energy, the temperature stays constant until all the substance has changed state. The substance continues absorbing energy throughout the process.

questions.stem: A heating curve shows temperature plotted against time for a substance being heated. What do the flat sections of the curve represent?

options.text: No energy being transferred to the substance

questions.explanation: Flat sections on a heating curve show periods where the temperature is constant despite continuous heating. This occurs during changes of state (melting or boiling) because energy is used to overcome intermolecular forces rather than raise the temperature. The sloped sections show the substance's temperature rising within a single state.

questions.stem: Water is heated from ice at -10 degrees C to steam at 120 degrees C. How many changes of state occur during this process?
questions.explanation: Two changes of state occur: melting (ice to liquid water at 0 degrees C) and boiling/evaporation (liquid water to steam at 100 degrees C). Each change of state involves a flat section on the heating curve where temperature remains constant while energy breaks intermolecular bonds.

questions.stem: On a cold morning, water droplets form on the outside of a cold window. What change of state is occurring?
questions.explanation: Water vapour in the warm air contacts the cold window surface and loses energy. The gas particles slow down enough for intermolecular forces to pull them together, forming liquid droplets. This gas-to-liquid change is condensation. Evaporation is the reverse (liquid to gas). Sublimation is solid directly to gas.

questions.stem: An impure substance melts over a range of temperatures rather than at a sharp melting point. A student tests an unknown solid and finds it melts between 75 degrees C and 82 degrees C. What can the student conclude?

options.text: The substance is pure with a melting point of 75 degrees C
The substance is a mixture or contains impurities
The substance must be an element

questions.explanation: Pure substances have sharp, well-defined melting points. A substance that melts over a range of temperatures (75-82 degrees C) contains impurities or is a mixture. Impurities disrupt the regular structure, meaning different parts of the substance require different amounts of energy to melt. This is a standard purity test in chemistry.
